name: Baking soda brushing

lead: Baking soda brushing means cleaning teeth with sodium bicarbonate, either as a commercial toothpaste that contains it or as a home-made paste. People use it to lift surface stains from coffee, tea and tobacco.

A review summarised on Wikipedia describes baking soda as a low-abrasive and effective stain remover with no adverse effects reported in clinical studies, though that comes from a single review. Clinical trials of commercial baking soda toothpastes have mostly measured plaque removal rather than whitening.

paras: Sodium bicarbonate is a mild abrasive that physically scrubs extrinsic stain and plaque. It also buffers acid, which has been proposed to help against acid-loving bacteria such as Streptococcus mutans.

Baking soda is low in abrasiveness compared with many abrasives, and clinical reports of harm are limited. It does not bleach the tooth, and most evidence concerns commercial formulations rather than do-it-yourself pastes, whose texture and frequency of use vary.

lead: Baking soda brushing is the practice of cleaning teeth with sodium bicarbonate, either through commercial toothpastes that contain it or as a home-made paste, usually to remove surface stain. Sodium bicarbonate is also used as an ingredient in some mouthwashes, where it is described as having anticaries and abrasive properties [1].

A 2017 review reported on the Wikipedia tooth-whitening page describes baking soda as a low-abrasive, effective stain remover whose buffering properties may help against Streptococcus mutans, with no adverse effects reported in clinical studies; the page notes this rests on a single review [2].

Controlled human studies mainly concern commercial baking soda dentifrices and plaque removal. A 2008 report of five clinical studies compared baking soda toothpastes with non-baking-soda formulations on plaque removal [3].

paras: Sodium bicarbonate is a white powder used widely in cooking and cleaning. In oral care it appears in commercial toothpastes and mouthwashes, and some people mix it with water to make a paste for brushing [1].

In looksmaxxing and tooth-care circles baking soda is one of several low-cost do-it-yourself approaches to removing stain. It is often combined with other household ingredients, which are covered in separate entries.

The Wikipedia tooth-whitening page, citing a 2017 review, describes baking soda as an effective, low-abrasive stain remover [2]. Evidence for it as a whitening agent beyond surface stain is not established in the sources reviewed here, and it is not a bleaching agent.
Plaque removal has been better studied: five clinical studies reported in 2008 compared baking soda dentifrices with other commercial toothpastes for plaque removal [3].

The same review summary says clinical studies reported no adverse effects of baking soda toothpaste, though it rests on one source [2]. General dental guidance, as summarised on Wikipedia, notes that brushing too hard causes abrasion regardless of the paste [4].

A 2008 report in the Journal of Clinical Dentistry described five clinical studies comparing commercial baking soda dentifrices with non-baking-soda toothpastes for plaque removal [3]. No clinical trials of home-made baking soda pastes for whitening were identified.
